titulo: Info Matrix (Textos 07) — Cap. 7 / Final — Sessyoin Kiara e Andersen

linhas.en:
Three Great Authors of fairy tales known the world over……
Grimm, Aesop, Andersen……and among them,
he is the only one who wrote his original works.

Whereas others were collectors and editors who compiled
folklore, legends, and the like, he's the only one who made
new stories as an "author" in the truest sense of the word.

Such masterpieces include:
"The Little Match Girl," "The Little Mermaid,"
"The Emperor's New Clothes," "The Snow Queen,"
"The Ugly Duckling" as well as others.

In addition, it's said that the model for the "girl"
in "The Little Match Girl" was Andersen's mother,
who, though poor, worked without pause to send Andersen
through higher-level education and left the world
having never once experienced pleasure.
キーワード１偽名テキスト

Andersen's characteristic skill. Rank A.

The art of observing and understanding people.
It's not simply observing but also hypothesizing the
manners, likes, even the lives, of people he might not
even know the names of, requiring incredible memory.

Though Andersen is known as a pessimist,
the foundation of it isn't rejection but understanding.
The only thing he can do is spin stories,
and that's exactly why he swore
to continue to speak more sincerely than anyone else.

             ◆

He may criticize how BB and the Alter Egos go about love
as "unsightly," "in bad taste," and "conceited," but
beneath it is profound understanding and identification,
as well as reprimand.
It goes without saying that most of his abusive language
isn't to completely deny them, but to serve as
candid advice filled with warnings.

……well, that he hates woman is also an undeniable truth.
キーワード２偽名テキスト

The unpolished manuscript of Andersen's autobiography,
"The Fairy Tale of My Life."

To Andersen, who said "the majority of what I write are
projections of myself," "The Fairy Tale of My Life" is
the record of Andersen's way of life, which he compiled
as "the supreme annotation of all of my works."

To put it another way, it serves as a core manuscript
on the author Andersen's #ROFS0002#RUBS    alter ego#RUBEother self#REND―――
though to a writer, everything they write is an other self.

Every individual page of this book takes the mana provided
by people who love the author known as Andersen,
taking the shape of "the Andersen the readers see,"
and can take action by becoming that other self.

But that is not the truth worth of this Noble Phantasm.
Just as a writer produces a story, by wiping the book clean
and starting over from scratch, it becomes possible
to raise "a single person" to "a single main character."

The effect…… the degree of growth increases the farther
the manuscript progresses. With only several pages,
only a few coincidences may occur, but with all the pages……
in the event the manuscript is completed, its subject will
reach their "greatest form," just as they had imagined.

At a glance, it may look like an omnipotent Noble Phantasm,
but Andersen's deep-rooted, gloomy philosophy: "There is
no finale that brings happiness to humans besides death,"
resigned that "There's no way everything turns out well,"
and author's pride will not permit convenient developments,
won't allow someone to attain their "ideal form" so easily.

Of course, the quality of the "story" also depends
on Andersen's motivation. Essentially, it's impossible
to attain "that person's ultimate form" without
a subject that ignites considerable passion in him.
宝具・偽名のテキスト

A skill that accelerates magic incantations. In his case,
it seems to give a small boost to his writing speed
rather than his magic.

"The speed at which I write is slow. Before that,
  I basically have no motivation
  so there's no way I'd write professionally!"

says the person himself.
スキル１偽名テキスト

An indication of the extent gossip has distorted the truth,
regardless of the actual person's will or appearance.

In Andersen's case, it is the "Curse of the Readers."
His fairy tales becoming too well-known, Andersen's
original personality was painted over by the image of
an author of fairy tales.

As a Servant, Andersen's limbs are being corroded by
the images of the fairy tales that represent him. Though
hidden by his western-style clothing, the skin underneath
is afflicted by merman scales, match burns, and frostbite,
and when he speaks, his throat is sliced with intense pain.
スキル２偽名テキスト

The ability to construct various items through magecraft.
While he doesn't know magecraft, by making practical use
of his Noble Phantasm, he can more or less produce
what can be found in his literary works.

Apparently, his specialty is "a love letter that conveys
100% of your feelings" but considering Andersen's own
experience with love, it's pretty much impossible to ask.

             ◆

In addition, he had a strange habit when he was alive:

"While I'm sleeping, isn't it possible
  for me to be mistaken for dead and get buried?"

was his fear, and it's said that he was so anxious about it
that he always had a note with "I'm not dead" written on it
on his person.
スキル３偽名テキスト

A real person. Born in 1805, died in 1875 by liver cancer.
He's known as one of the Three Great Authors now,
but half his life was filled with setbacks and frustration.

Born as the son of a cobbler, he aspired to be an actor
but gave up without results. Then, he aimed to be a poet,
but received harsh criticism. Finally, a book he published
himself began to sell decently well, and with the profits,
took a trip abroad. On that trip, he found inspiration for
his breakthrough work, "The Improvisatore" and was
finally acknowledged by the world. He was 30.

Thereafter, he shifted to writing fairy tales,
but choosing to become an author of fairy tales
because they were liked better than his more
honest works, caused him only pain.

As if to represent that, his fairy tales are full of
violence, misfortune, poverty, and portrayed in a way
that sees death as salvation.

In the form of fairy tales, he continued to depict the
grief of desperate poverty and the hopelessness of
death as the only escape from it.
……all while masking the feelings swirling in his chest
with beautiful composition.


Still, even after gaining fame, he lived out his life as
a bachelor, without the company of women.
One theory is that there was someone he had feelings for,
but due to pride and a complex regarding his appearance,
he missed countless opportunities to confess.

He died of liver cancer at the age of 70.
It's said he died grasping a letter from his first love,
which he always had on his person.

             ◆

Of all things, when Andersen was summoned to the Moon Cell,
it was as a boy prior to becoming famous.

His alignment is Lawful Neutral.
His personality is introverted, self-assured, and passive.
As a glum, pessimistic poet, he has no intention of being
liked by others, and he lacks any intention of enjoying life
as he no longer sees any merit for him to find.
Andersen doesn't have a wish for the Holy Grail.
This may be because he didn't attain a single thing he
wished for when he was alive.

"That's assuming that life has value.
  I'd say it's worth less than human delusions!"

he says, acting as if he hates everything in the world.

"Well, even if I hate the world, it's not like I detest it.
  If there is something worth loving, then it'd be fine
  to light the hearth of frozen affection once again."

……what a troublesome man he is.

"I will depict your life.
  You truly are the ugliness of woman itself.
  It's a story that makes me want to vomit up everything."

             ◆

Andersen may perpetually criticize Kiara to her face,
but he's not a friend of #FAMILY #GIVEN either.
It's simply how his brand of impartiality shows itself.
As Andersen has the methodology of an author,
being helpful is his true nature.
To begin with, if one doesn't think to entertain,
to serve their readers, they're not fit to be a writer.

Andersen may be a hardened pessimist, but he wouldn't
laugh at the efforts of people who try to "live properly"
or "achieve something with everything they have."

Because he once dreamed for society to strive for that.

The reason Andersen advised #FAMILY #GIVEN,
who was trying to resolve the incident, even as he was
telling them "It's futile. Just leave those girls alone,"
and never completely denied Kiara, who was
worsening the situation, even while cursing her as
"Greedy, shameless, and on top of that, a liar!
 Only demons in a fairy tale could be as unsightly as you!"
is because both #FAMILY #GIVEN and Kiara were
earnestly "living their lives with everything they had."

             ◆

In the end.

"A final #RUBS     light#RUBEsentence#REND for that unrewarded life."

That is the foundation of this Servant.

Andersen, who became a world-renowned author,
yet never obtained even a single thing he desired.
The writer of fairy tales who, while speaking of love,
never once attained it. To him, "a life that will
fade away unrewarded in the end" is a story to be told.
People who find happiness easily are the same as
scenery to him. They can go be happy by themselves.


"I want to give a final light to the lives of people
abandoned even by God," is the core of Andersen's soul.

If you come to a stop on the final road,
and you can afford to turn around―――
you should be able to see a piece of this Servant's truth.
